extraction.narrative:
# DISCHARGE SUMMARY

**PATIENT INFORMATION**
Name: Jane Doe
Age: 58 years
Sex: Female
Medical Record Number: 98765
Admission Date: November 8, 2024
Surgery Date: November 8, 2024 (emergent)
Discharge Date: November 20, 2024
Length of Stay: 13 days

**DIAGNOSES**
Primary: Large left middle cerebral artery (MCA) territory infarct with significant mass effect

**HOSPITAL COURSE**

Ms. Doe is a 58-year-old female who presented to the emergency department on November 8, 2024, with sudden onset right-sided hemiparesis and expressive aphasia. On admission, her Glasgow Coma Scale was 13 (E4V3M6) with right arm and leg weakness graded at 2/5 strength. Computed tomography of the head revealed a large left MCA territory infarct with significant mass effect and 8mm midline shift.

Given the extent of the infarct and associated mass effect, the patient was taken emergently to the operating room on the day of admission for left decompressive hemicraniectomy with duraplasty. The bone flap was removed and duraplasty was performed without intraoperative complications. Estimated blood loss was 200ml.

Post-operatively, the patient was managed in the intensive care unit. On post-operative day 1, she remained intubated with a Glasgow Coma Scale of 10T (E3VTM6). An intracranial pressure monitor was placed, with pressures ranging from 12-18 mmHg, which remained within normal limits throughout monitoring. Right hemiparesis persisted at 2/5 strength. The patient was successfully extubated on post-operative day 3, at which time her Glasgow Coma Scale improved to 13 (E4V3M6). She was following simple commands, though right-sided weakness remained unchanged.

By post-operative day 7, the patient demonstrated significant neurological improvement and was transferred from the intensive care unit to the floor. Her Glasgow Coma Scale was 15 (E4V5M6), and while expressive aphasia persisted, notable improvement was observed. Motor strength had improved to 3/5 in the right arm and 3+/5 in the right leg. Physical therapy and occupational therapy began working intensively with the patient.

The patient continued to make steady functional gains throughout the remainder of her hospitalization. By post-operative day 12, she demonstrated significant functional improvement, ambulating 50 feet independently with a walker. Speech continued to improve daily. Motor strength had further improved to 4-/5 in the right arm and 4/5 in the right leg. The patient was medically stable and cleared for discharge to an acute rehabilitation facility.

**DISCHARGE STATUS**

Neurological Examination: The patient is alert and oriented to person, place, and time. She demonstrates mild expressive aphasia but is able to follow all commands appropriately. Motor examination reveals right arm strength of 4-/5 and right leg strength of 4/5. Glasgow Coma Scale is 15 (E4V5M6).

Functional Status: The patient is ambulating independently with a walker. Karnofsky Performance Status is estimated at 70. Modified Rankin Scale score is 3, reflecting moderate disability with ability to walk unassisted with assistive device. ECOG Performance Status is 2.

**DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS**
1. Aspirin 325mg by mouth daily
2. Levetiracetam (Keppra) 1000mg by mouth twice daily
3. Atorvastatin 80mg by mouth daily
4. Metoprolol 25mg by mouth twice daily

**FOLLOW-UP**
1. Neurosurgery clinic appointment in 2 weeks post-discharge
2. Cranioplasty planned in 3 months

**DISCHARGE DISPOSITION**
Acute rehabilitation facility
